clue.text: Hard part about shrink reforming member of sect

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: about here means going around, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a part of a place is an area

indicators.note: reforming a thing remakes it in a new shape, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough job involving a psychiatrist reforming a cult member.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit inside AREA between its E and final A, after the opening H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hare Krishnas are followers of a Hindu devotional movement, often described as a religious sect.

clue.text: Commotion in photo shoot as only prime locations are needed

indicators.note: only the letters at prime-numbered positions (second, third, fifth and so on) are kept

parts.note: letters 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 of these three words

explanation.surface: A fuss at a photo shoot where only the best spots will do.
explanation.walkthrough: Prime locations sounds like choice sites for the shoot, but it means the prime-numbered letter positions.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is an informal word for a noisy fuss or uproar.

clue.text: Wine drinking ceremony about to be withdrawn

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the wine word swallows the other piece

parts.note: red is a kind of wine

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the ceremony word is read backwards

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony; turned round it gives ETIR

explanation.surface: Someone drinking wine at a ceremony is about to be removed from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired can describe someone who has withdrawn, from work or from company, to rest.

clue.text: Secure vehicle for Spooner's trip?

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: to stick is to secure, and a cart is a vehicle; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: Fixing a vehicle in place, as if ready for a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Trip is the definition in its switch sense: to trip a mechanism is to set it going, as a kick-start does.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip something is to activate or set it off, which is what a kick-start does to an engine or a process.

clue.text: Probably hash I inhaled — I'll look

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to mess it up, so the letters that follow get jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cannabis smoker admits they probably inhaled and will check.
explanation.walkthrough: Hash looks like cannabis in the surface, but it is the signal to mix up the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the phrase and the adverb express that something is very likely to be true.

clue.text: Dodgy leaseholder fine making European college students live here

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the letters are put into a crooked order
making one thing into another means one letter of fine is swapped for a different one

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before its E is swapped
E is the abbreviation for European
C is an abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A crooked landlord's penalty turns a continental college into student digs.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of FINE becomes C (European made into college) and the result is mixed up with LEASEHOLDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall of residence is a university building providing accommodation for students.

clue.text: Talisman not starting tie?

indicators.note: not starting tells you to drop the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a mascot is a lucky charm or talisman

explanation.surface: A lucky charm that fails to begin, perhaps in a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: Tie suggests a drawn game, but it is neckwear; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neckcloth, one kind of tie, named after the racecourse.

clue.text: Who bought nurses rings?

definitions.note: a hob is the cooker top that carries the rings, so this is a loose definition flagged by the question mark

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the phrase before it cradles the answer

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A question about which nurse purchased some jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: Nurses and rings conjure a hospital and jewellery, but rings here are the burners of a cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A hob is the flat top of a cooker fitted with gas or electric rings for cooking.

clue.text: Quarry ordered buffet menu for example

parts.note: to buffet is to strike or hit
a menu is an example of a list

explanation.surface: Someone choosing items from a buffet menu, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffet suggests a spread of food, but it is the verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit list sets out, in order, the targets someone intends to pursue, which are their quarry.

clue.text: Possible outcome of abusing debit card?

definitions.text: Possible outcome of abusing debit card?

indicators.note: abusing something mistreats it, so the letters it governs are knocked out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that misusing a bank card may harm your financial record.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: misuse your debit card and this follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspending on a card can damage a borrowing record, leaving a person with a poor credit rating.

clue.text: Bell's found here sometimes work with jerk

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A bell rings at work now and then with a sudden jolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Bell's is a brand of Scotch whisky, not a bell; in pubs spirits are poured through a measured dispenser fixed to the upturned bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: An optic is the pub dispenser attached to an inverted spirit bottle, where a whisky like Bell's is often fitted.

clue.text: Earmarked pub and time to meet after both cycling different amounts

indicators.note: cycling moves letters from the front of each word round to the back, by a different number for each

parts.note: a local is one's regular pub; move three letters to the end
a date is an arranged time to meet; move one letter to the end

explanation.surface: A pub and time reserved for meeting after a bike ride of differing distances.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British for one's neighbourhood pub. LOCAL becomes ALLOC and DATE becomes ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Allocated and earmarked both mean set aside or assigned for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Disperse a looser spray

indicators.note: dispersing scatters things, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to spread a spray more loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised can that releases its contents as a fine mist.

clue.text: Statistical oddity revealed by storyteller on the radio

parts.note: a secret that is revealed is out

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so go by pronunciation

parts.note: a storyteller in the sense of a fibber

explanation.surface: A strange statistic exposed by a radio storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: Storyteller here means someone who tells stories in the sense of fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics an outlier is a data point lying far from the rest, an anomaly in the set.

clue.text: Home help returning to country

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the help word is written backwards

parts.note: aid means help; it is turned round

explanation.surface: A domestic helper going back to their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Home help is a British term for a domestic carer, but here the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large country in South Asia.

clue.text: Sinister old soldier clubs gangster senseless

parts.note: ill can mean evil or harmful, as in ill omen
O is an abbreviation for old
a GI is an American soldier
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
Al Capone is crosswords' standard gangster

explanation.surface: A menacing veteran beats a gangster unconscious.
explanation.walkthrough: Senseless looks like knocked out in the surface, but it is the definition meaning irrational.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illogical lacks sound reasoning, so it makes no sense.

clue.text: Angry tirade assuming machinery gets wet

definitions.note: wet is read as a past-tense verb here, as in 'they wet the fields', so it matches the past participle

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so one piece takes the other inside it
an angry outburst is wild and disordered, so the letters next to it are thrown about

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a rig is apparatus or machinery, as in an oil rig

explanation.surface: A furious rant about equipment that has been soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: Angry reads as describing the tirade, but it signals the rearrangement; RIG goes in after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate land is to supply it with water, so irrigated means wet in the past tense.

clue.text: Smooth steps as Dell Technologies finally acquires satellite

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so the satellite goes inside

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded hollow, much like a glade

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of this word
the ISS, the International Space Station, is a satellite

explanation.surface: A computer firm's progress described as smooth after it buys a satellite company.
explanation.walkthrough: Dell Technologies reads as one company name; split it, a dell being a hollow among trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Glissades are gliding steps in ballet, and also smooth controlled slides down a snowy slope.

clue.text: Levity without admitting blasted thing

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: less means without, as in a sugarless tea

indicators.note: something blasted is blown apart, so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Joking around, without confessing to that wretched thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Blasted looks like a mild curse on the thing, but it is the signal to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is light-heartedness or a lack of seriousness, which is what lightness of mood conveys.

clue.text: Gathered Greek leader's opposite number is touring university

parts.note: GR is an abbreviation for Greek

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the outer piece goes around the university letter

parts.note: a newspaper's leader is its editorial; the op-ed page sits opposite it
U is an abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A Greek prime minister's counterpart visits a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Leader's opposite number reads as a rival politician, but a leader is a newspaper editorial and op-ed means the page opposite it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grouped and gathered both mean brought together into a collection or cluster.

clue.text: I perform in theatre bar

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the theatre abbreviation

parts.note: the NT is London's National Theatre
to go is to function or perform, as an engine goes

explanation.surface: An actor boasting of performing at the theatre bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre bar looks like a place to drink, but bar is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block or bar of cast metal, typically gold or silver.

clue.text: Get one from A Night at the Opera — or cough up

definitions.text: one from A Night at the Opera

indicators.note: up in the sense of stirred or messed up, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Grab a ticket to the opera, or cough up the money.
explanation.walkthrough: A Night at the Opera is the 1935 Marx Brothers film, not an evening out.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho Marx starred in the film A Night at the Opera alongside his brothers.

clue.text: Saw me leaving with trendy cycling food

indicators.note: cycling moves letters from the front of the word round to its end
leaving means going away, so those letters depart from the saying

parts.note: a saw is a saying, as is a gnome
taken as written, then removed
chic means stylish or trendy; move its last letter to the front

explanation.surface: Someone leaving after a fashionable bike ride, pausing for a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Saw and gnome are both rare words for a proverb or maxim.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings, made from potato or semolina, eaten as food.

clue.text: To begin with, cook sausage and porridge

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: its first letter
a link is one sausage in a chain

explanation.surface: Breakfast instructions: first cook a sausage, then the porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for time in prison, not the breakfast oats.
explanation.definitionFit: Clink is slang for prison, and porridge is slang for a prison sentence, so both mean doing time.

clue.text: Abruptly leave a pipe down inside shed

indicators.note: inside places the first pieces within the shed word

parts.note: to doff is to take off or shed, as a hat
taken as written
sh is the call to be quiet, to pipe down

explanation.surface: Someone told to keep quiet in the garden shed storms off.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed reads as a garden hut but is the verb meaning take off.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash off is to leave hurriedly and suddenly.

clue.text: Absurdity of Farage making case for axing head of Coutts

indicators.note: making one thing into another means one chunk of the name is replaced

parts.note: the politician's surname taken as written

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of this word, which are swapped out

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter, which goes in their place

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage's public complaint after the private bank Coutts closed his account, called a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as: Farage, making the case of axing into the head of Coutts, so AG in the name becomes C.
explanation.definitionFit: A farce is a ridiculous situation or proceeding, an absurdity.

clue.text: Sign top hat's timeless

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: less means without, so the word reads as without the time letter, which is dropped from the hat

parts.note: a tricorn is a three-cornered hat
T is the abbreviation for time; it is removed

explanation.surface: A sign that the top hat never goes out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Top hat reads as one item, but top and hat are separate pieces, and timeless splits too.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, the goat.

clue.text: Dye's covering my furnishings etc

indicators.note: the covering of a word is its outer layer, the first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of dye
cor and my are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Paint covering one's home furnishings.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the overall style of a room's furnishings, paint and ornament.

clue.text: In Cannes the director's debut was winning

parts.note: le is French for the, as spoken in Cannes

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so take the opening letter

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A director's first film was a winner at Cannes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cannes film festival makes debut look like a first film, but it picks a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have led is to have been in front, which is to have been winning.

clue.text: Perhaps organ stopper's occasionally hidden within foundation?

indicators.note: within places the chosen letters inside the foundation word

parts.note: a keystone is a founding principle on which all else rests

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so take every other letter

parts.note: its second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: An organ stopper is sometimes concealed in the base of the instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Organ and stopper suggest a pipe organ's stops, but the organ is a body part and the stopper something that blocks it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidney stone is a hard mineral deposit that can block the kidney, an organ, perhaps.
